newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc finishes week just off strong rally highs.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc finishes week just off strong rally highs.

text.p: Zinc prices charged to near seven-year highs on Friday and nickel bounced more than $100, but the other metals finished the week with a whimper.
Fresh speculative interest tipped zinc over the tough $1,400 mark in inter-office trading ahead of the afternoon session on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
Building on gains earlier this week, zinc achieved a top price of $1,405 -- the highest level since October 1990.
But end-of-week profit-taking pared some of its gains and three months metal ended slightly lower at $1,399 by the end of the kerb, still up $6 from Thursday's finish.
"Zinc looks very good. It's done quite a lot this week and it's not surprising to see a little profit taking towards the end of the week," said analyst William Adams of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
Nickel picked up towards the end of the trading day finishing $110 stronger at $7,270, the day's high.
Prices bounced sharply on shortcovering after probing support just below the day's low of $7,130, analysts said.
Traders said the market was closely watching developments at the strike-bound Inco Sudbury facilities.
The union said late on Thursday that they did not expect developments until after the July maintenance closure.
Flagship copper, meanwhile, failed to broach the key $2,600 resistance level early in the day.
It subsequently sank during the kerb to end near the day's low at $2,567, compared to Thursday's $2,585.50.
"The copper market was not about three-months prices, it's about the spread," Adams said.
The cash to threes backwardation continued to flare out, hitting a high of around $140 at one point, compared to around $115 on Thursday.
Dealers said the change stemmed from positions being rolled forward.
The other metals were mostly quiet and finished easier.
Aluminium was disheartend by lack of progress towards $1,600 resistance and ended the week $6 easier at $1,578.
Quiet lead was last indicated at $622/623, compared to $624, while tin was off $25 at $5,590.
Alloy was last indicated slightly easier at $1,465/1,470.
